title: Love Among Believers
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Love among believers is the Christlike care, patience, sacrifice, truthfulness, forgiveness, and service that God commands within His church. This love is a mark of true discipleship.
summary: Love among believers is the Christlike care, patience, sacrifice, truthfulness, forgiveness, and service that God commands within His church. This love is a mark of true discipleship.
christFocus: Jesus Christ loved His people by laying down His life for them. The church learns love from His cross, His patience, His mercy, and His command to love one another as He loved us.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus commanded His disciples to love one another as He loved them. This love is not vague kindness or sentimental words; it is sacrificial, truthful, patient, and practical.

Love among believers displays the Gospel. The world is meant to see Christ’s disciples marked by a love that comes from Him and reflects His character.

Scripture calls believers to love in deed and truth. Love forgives, serves, bears with weakness, covers offenses rightly, confronts when necessary, and seeks the good of others.

This love is impossible apart from God’s grace. Believers love because God first loved them, and because the Spirit forms Christlike character in the people of God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Churches may have correct doctrine and active programs while lacking visible love. Without love, truth can be wielded harshly and service can become performance.

This doctrine also speaks to those who have experienced rejection. Christ’s church should be a place where redeemed people learn to love with patience, holiness, and sacrificial care.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Practice love in concrete ways. Speak truthfully, forgive quickly, serve quietly, bear patiently, and move toward those in need. Do not reduce love to words or feelings; let the love of Christ shape how you treat His people.
